cards.title: Clienti: list with search and filter at /clienti, plus a client detail route, both under the density doctrine.
cards.plain: A Customers section appears in the menu: a searchable list that shows only what is needed to pick the right one, and a page per customer holding everything the business knows about them.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/clients.spec.ts` exits 0. clients.spec covers: the list renders rows from the database and no mock; searching by name matches without diacritics and without case; searching by IDNO matches exactly; the active filter hides deactivated clients and the "toate" filter shows them; the list paginates at 25 and does not render an unbounded table; clicking a row opens the client detail route and the browser back button returns to the list with the search term intact; creating a client persists and survives a reload; a duplicate IDNO is refused with a Romanian message; every visible string on both screens is Romanian. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build` exits 0. PLUS COMMAND: `npm run check:migrations` exits 0, which runs scripts/poc-free/local-db/assertions/0020_search_clients.sql against a real PostgreSQL. It RAISES on: more or fewer than one public.search_clients; the default not being active-only; "tigla" not finding a name spelled with diacritics; a search with diacritics and capitals not finding it either; a search by IDNO, by phone or by email not finding its one row; a search matching nothing returning rows anyway; either filter returning the wrong count; an UNKNOWN status not falling back to active; the open-project count including a closed or deactivated project or excluding a suspended one; a one-row page not carrying the correct total; two pages of two not covering four distinct clients exactly once; an offset past the end erroring instead of returning nothing; or the ordering not being by name case-insensitively. THE SPEC PROVES THE SCREEN AND THE ASSERTIONS PROVE THE QUERY. The folding, the four searchable columns, the pagination arithmetic and the window-function total are the parts a browser test can only see indirectly, and the parts most likely to be subtly wrong. THE MIGRATION IS AUTHORED AND NOT APPLIED, per R-062: supabase/migrations/0020_search_clients.sql is in the pending register and the apply is P3-27.
cards.defaults: THE LIST IS ONE RPC AND NOT A POSTGREST QUERY, AND THAT IS FORCED BY THE FOLD. P3-06 asks for one search box, diacritic-folded, filtered SERVER SIDE. PostgREST filters name columns, not expressions, so `fold_text.ilike...` is not a thing it can send, and `ilike` over the raw column does not match "Țiglă" when somebody types "tigla" - which is the exact defect phase 1 found on screen and wrote into docs/LEARNINGS.md. public.search_clients in migration 0020 keeps ONE definition of the fold, the one 0017 created, so what the search box finds and what a backfill matches cannot disagree. THE TOTAL COMES BACK WITH EVERY PAGE, as a window function over the filtered set. A separate count query is a second round trip that can disagree with the first under concurrent writes, and the footer would then claim a number of pages the list cannot produce. THE OPEN-PROJECT COUNT IS IN THE SAME PASS, which is the fifth of the five columns. Counting it per row afterwards is a query per page at best and a query per row at worst. OPEN MEANS NOT CLOSED AND NOT DEACTIVATED, AND SUSPENDED COUNTS. A stopped site is still a relationship in progress; leaving it out would make the column say a client has no work with the firm. AN UNKNOWN FILTER VALUE FALLS BACK TO THE DEFAULT AND DOES NOT ERROR. Somebody sends a stale link with ?stare=nonsense or ?pagina=abc and gets a list, not an error page. Both the SQL and parseClientQuery do this, deliberately, at both ends. THE ROLE GATE IS IN THE SCREEN AND IN THE ACTION, and neither is the real one: the policies in 0013 are owner-only and refuse the write at the database. The screen hides the button because P3-06 says an interface that offers a button the database will refuse is the defect; the action re-checks because a server action is reachable without the screen. ROUTES: /clienti for the list and /clienti/[id] for the detail, added to lib/nav.ts under a new "Relatii" group together with Proiecte. lib/nav.ts is the single definition of navigation and the dead-link check reads it, so a route that is not in it does not exist. THE LIST SHOWS FIVE COLUMNS AND NOT ONE MORE: Denumire, Tip, Telefon, Proiecte active (a count), Stare. Address, email, IDNO and notes are detail, not list. This is the density doctrine applied and it is not negotiable per screen. SEARCH IS ONE BOX over name, IDNO, phone and email, diacritic-folded and case-folded, debounced, filtering server side. Not four separate filter inputs. FILTERS ARE TWO CONTROLS: type (toate, companie, persoana fizica) and status (active, inactive, toate), defaulting to active. Every filter is in the URL query string so a filtered list can be sent to somebody as a link and so the back button restores it. DETAIL IS A ROUTE, NOT A PANEL, because it carries tabs in the next card and a side panel cannot hold five tabs at a readable width on a desktop screen. The orders and inventory screens keep their existing side panels; this is not a change to them. CREATE AND EDIT ARE OWNER-ONLY IN THE UI because the RLS policies are owner-only. The account manager sees the list and the detail and gets a Romanian explanation rather than a form that saves nothing. A UI that offers a button the database will refuse is the defect, not the policy. DENSITY DOCTRINE BINDS THIS CARD. Summary first, detail behind a drill-in. A full-length table is never dumped into a page. A list surface shows the smallest set of columns that lets a person choose a row, and everything else lives on the row detail. THE NUMBERS, SO THAT "COMPACT" IS NOT A MATTER OF TASTE: a summary block on a page that is not itself a list shows AT MOST 5 ROWS and carries a link to the full history. A list page paginates at 25 rows and never renders an unbounded table. A row detail opens in the existing side panel pattern where one already exists on that screen, and as a route otherwise. DESKTOP FIRST. Responsive and mobile layouts are out of scope, per CLAUDE.md section 11. cards.title: Necesar de materiale: for projects in lead, offer, contract or active with an ACCEPTED deviz, what they still need after what has already been issued, against current stock.
cards.plain: For every job that is quoted, signed or under way, the system works out what material is still to come, subtracts what has already gone out to site, and compares the rest with what is in the warehouse. It is the difference between buying ahead and reacting to an empty shelf.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/procurement.spec.ts` exits 0. procurement.spec covers: projects whose status is lead, offer, contract OR active and which carry a current ACCEPTED deviz are included, and A PROJECT IN active WITH AN ACCEPTED DEVIZ IS INCLUDED; a project in suspended or closed is excluded even with an accepted deviz; a project whose only deviz is draft, sent, rejected or expired is EXCLUDED and is reported in the excluded count, because only accepted feeds this screen; a project with no deviz at all is excluded and is REPORTED in a Romanian count of excluded projects rather than silently omitted, with a link to them; the required quantity per product is the sum of accepted-deviz line quantities across the included projects MINUS the quantity already issued to those projects for that product, floored at zero; a project whose issued quantity for a product already exceeds its estimate contributes zero for that product and not a negative number; the shortfall is required minus current stock, floored at zero, and a product with enough stock shows no shortfall; a product required by two projects aggregates to one row and the contributing projects are shown per row; the requirement is broken down by project status and is NOT weighted by probability; every visible string is Romanian. cards.title: Schema and module: outbound_lines freezes the unit value at the moment of issue, so a project cost total stops moving when somebody edits a product price.
cards.plain: A job's material cost is worked out from today's product prices, so changing a price silently rewrites what past jobs appear to have cost. This records the price onto the release at the moment it happens, the way an invoice does, and the warning currently printed on the screen comes off.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/project-cost-snapshot.spec.ts` exits 0. The spec covers, and the second case is the whole card: an issue is created against a project and the project cost total is read; the product's `unit_value_mdl` is then changed in the catalogue; the project cost total is UNCHANGED, to the leu, on both the total and the by-product breakdown; a NEW issue of the SAME product raised after the price change is costed at the NEW value, so one project legitimately holds two different unit values for one product and the total is their sum; a row issued before this migration still carries a value and is not null and not zero; and the Romanian footnote naming the current-catalogue caveat is GONE from the Cost tab, because it has stopped being true. PLUS `ls supabase/migrations/*_outbound_unit_value_at_issue.sql` exits 0, and `npm run check:migrations` exits 0 with that file in the set applied to the bare postgres.
cards.defaults:
THE COLUMN IS `unit_value_at_issue_mdl` ON `public.outbound_lines`, numeric(14,2) not null check (>= 0). The name is the one the AUTHOR wrote on P3-11 and it carries the currency suffix every other money column in this schema carries (unit_value_mdl, sale_price_mdl, budget_mdl, unit_price_mdl).

NOT NULL WITH A BACKFILL, NEVER NULLABLE WITH A FALLBACK. Add the column nullable, backfill every existing row from products.unit_value_mdl, then set not null in the same migration and the same transaction. A nullable column read as `coalesce(unit_value_at_issue_mdl, p.unit_value_mdl)` is a default-and-override, not a snapshot: it is indistinguishable from correct on the day it is built and diverges silently afterwards. R-058 named exactly that shape on the deviz price and rejected it, and the same reasoning binds here.

THE BACKFILL IS HONEST ABOUT WHAT IT CANNOT KNOW, IN A COMMENT IN THE FILE. Rows issued before this migration get today's catalogue value because no other value has ever existed. That is not a repair of history and the comment says so: this card freezes the value from now on, and the rows it backfills keep whatever drift they already had.

cards.defaults: THE DECLARATION IS A MACHINE-READ LINE IN THE MIGRATION FILE ITSELF, not a flag on the command line and not an environment variable, because the grant in CLAUDE.md 8.6 rests on the script deciding rather than the terminal choosing, and anything a terminal can pass at the prompt is a choice. THE ABSOLUTE EXCLUSION IS UNTOUCHED: DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE and DELETE stay refused with nothing executed, and no declaration reaches them.
